examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: возвращаться домой = to come back home; к + dative = to someone

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.
examples.trans: Remember: evil always comes back to the ruler.

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать').

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: + genitive.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: Contrast дома = at home.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: жить на зарплату = to live on one's salary

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович учёный, и он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich is a scholar, and he lives on a salary.

meanings.note: Made of gold or gold-coloured.
'золотые руки' = skilled hands.

examples.trans: He's very good with his hands.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: + genitive.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините.
+ accusative (кого).

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, excuse me, there's someone here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: В любой момент = at any moment.

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Uncountable, singular only.
+ infinitive.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

никак.gloss: in no way, not at all

meanings.note: Никак не могу = I just can't.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

определиться.gloss: to make up one's mind, to decide

meanings.en: to make up one's mind, decide
meanings.note: определиться с чем-то = decide on something

examples.text: С цветом никак не могу определиться.
examples.trans: I just can't decide on the colour.

examples.text: То есть он не определился до сих пор?
examples.trans: So he still hasn't made up his mind?

meanings.note: + dative of the person.

examples.text: Прости, я должен ответить. Да, Аллочка!
examples.trans: Sorry, I have to answer this. Yes, Allochka!

meanings.note: declines like a feminine noun in -а, but is masculine

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: letters, books, reports
писать картины

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить').

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звать').

examples.text: Дядя Аркадий всё починит и позовёт.
examples.trans: Uncle Arkady will fix everything and call you.

examples.text: Я просил позвать сомелье, а не буфетчика!
examples.trans: I asked you to call the sommelier, not the barman!

examples.text: Главное, чтобы она не позвала директора.
examples.trans: The main thing is that she doesn't call the director.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу. Что, плохая работа?
examples.trans: But you were offered a job. What, is it a bad job?

meanings.note: imperative прощай(те) = farewell

examples.trans: Oh, all right, I forgive you.

examples.text: Потому что фугу никогда не прощает ошибок.

examples.trans: To love is the great art of forgiving.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I already poured that wine down the sink, Max!
Do you mind that this is our sink?

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Of a door, bag, etc.
Diminutive of рука.

examples.trans: Yulia, bring a pen and a piece of paper.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать').

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Used as imperative exhortation.
Comparison.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Спокойной ночи = good night. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm, quiet').
Спокойной ночи = good night. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm, quiet').

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!
examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by. Good night!

meanings.note: Irregular plural стулья.

examples.trans: Put the chair by the table.

examples.text: А зачем нам бревно? Я вот стулья взял!
examples.trans: Why do we need a log? I brought chairs, look!

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives
Я считаю, что... = I think that. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to count; to think, to consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun.

examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.
